seeds.header: Introduction: The Failure of the Word as a Label
seeds.text: This foundation is broken.
derivation_wave_sample: For centuries, conventional linguistics has treated words as arbitrary labels—sounds and symbols agreed upon by social habit, floating detached in an abstract realm of signs.
Under this view, language is merely a code used by humans to name things, describe thoughts, and trade opinions.

seeds.header: Introduction: The Failure of the Word as a Label
seeds.text: It is an operational formula that records how an applied force overcomes resistance to produce a measurable change in the world.
derivation_wave_sample: > **Language is event physics.** A word is not a label pinned to a static object; it is a purpose-built tool invented by an acting agent to resolve a specific strain in reality.
A word does not exist in a vacuum.

seeds.header: 1. The Four Language Axioms
seeds.text: **Axiom I (Event Primacy):** Words describe actions and events, not static objects.
derivation_wave_sample: To understand how words work, language must be grounded in physical and informational reality:

seeds.header: 1. The Four Language Axioms
seeds.text: **Axiom II (Contextual Framing):** Language operates by tracking actions within a defined contextual frame.

seeds.header: 1. The Four Language Axioms
seeds.text: **Axiom III (Physical Anchoring):** Words are ultimately rooted in physical constraint, not arbitrary agreement.

seeds.header: 1. The Four Language Axioms
seeds.text: **Axiom IV (Competence as Literacy):** True literacy is competence in the world, not the mere decoding of written symbols.

seeds.text: To survive and build, the agent must apply effort to change that disordered state into an ordered state.
